decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up left approach to the left tube, lifting and turning the open gripper toward its visible axis.
Advance left open gripper above the tube while completing the downward approach orientation; retain elbow-up continuity.
Lower to the left tube with an approximately vertical grasp axis; use the next wrist view to refine centering before closing.
Refine left tube axis and centering from the wrist view, then close around the body; retention is not yet established.
Lift the closed left gripper and tube clear of the table, checking visible retention before transfer.
Tube remains visibly retained. Begin gradual upright rotation and carry toward the left rack slot, keeping the gripper closed.
Continue smooth upright rotation and move the retained tube above the left side of the rack.
Finish making the tube upright above the left rack opening; pause at clearance height for alignment.
Lower the upright retained tube toward the left large slot, using a slow final approach and keeping the gripper closed.
Make the final small centering correction and insert the first tube slowly to rack depth; keep holding until its seating is visible.
Open the left gripper at insertion depth and withdraw gently to verify that the first tube remains upright in its slot.
First tube is standing after release. Retract the left arm while beginning an elbow-up, open-gripper approach to the outer right tube.
Return the empty left arm toward origin and advance the right gripper above the outer tube, gradually turning downward without changing elbow branch.
Finish left return and lower the right open gripper to the outer tube, correcting its yaw to match the visible cap-to-tip direction.
Make a small wrist-based axis correction at the outer right tube, then close around its body and pause before lifting.
Lift the second tube clear while keeping the right gripper closed; verify that it follows the hand before carrying it to the rack.
The second tube follows the right hand. Carry it inward above the table while rotating it toward upright and a right-side rack approach.
Continue the second tube's smooth inward transfer and upright rotation, maintaining clearance and a closed right gripper.
Finish orienting the retained second tube upright above the right large rack slot and slow for visual alignment.
Lower the second upright tube toward the right rack slot while maintaining the closed grasp and watching alignment.
Apply a millimeter-scale centering correction and gently seat the second tube to rack depth, keeping the right gripper closed.
The tube appears to have slid upward rather than seated. Lift slightly to clear the rim and recenter inward/forward before another gentle insertion.
Retry a slow vertical insertion after recentering. The tube is held lower on its body, so assess visible seating rather than EE height alone.
Lower a little farther, then open at the slot to let the tube settle without pushing the gripper into the rack; verify its final upright position.
The released second tube has settled upright. Withdraw the open right hand upward and back, clearing the rack before approaching the last tube.
Both released tubes remain upright. Raise and rotate the right open gripper toward the remaining tube, keeping clear of the rack.
Advance above the last tube while continuing the gradual downward wrist rotation; leave grasping clearance for visual refinement.
Finish the downward orientation and lower the open right gripper toward the last tube; check centering in the wrist view before closing.
Align the right gripper with the last tube's visible tilt, make a small centering/descent correction, and close around its body.
Lift the last tube away from the table with the right gripper closed; check retention and axis alignment before moving to the rack.
The last tube is retained and centered in the hand. Begin an elevated transfer toward the middle rack opening while gradually rotating upright.
Continue the elevated inward transfer and upright rotation of the third tube, avoiding the two seated tubes.
Finish the third tube's upright orientation above the middle slot, slowing down for alignment and maintaining a closed grasp.
Lower the third upright tube toward the middle opening with a small centering correction; keep it closed and inspect before the final seating motion.
The descent shows contact/tracking resistance near a neighboring tube. Lift and turn to a more frontal middle-slot approach, keeping the last tube upright and held.
Retry the third tube's descent from the more frontal approach, maintaining upright alignment over the central opening and watching for contact.
The frontal descent is tracking freely. Gently lower the third tube the remaining distance into the central slot, keeping its grasp closed until seating is visible.
The third tube has slid in the grasp against the slot rim. Lift slightly and shift forward by a centimeter to recenter its tip before retrying insertion.
Retry a slow vertical seating motion with the third tube now recentered, avoiding lateral motion while its tip enters the opening.
Open at the central slot without further downward pressure so the third tube can settle, then inspect its upright position and depth.
Withdraw the open hand slightly to inspect the third tube without gripper occlusion; its cap still appears higher than the other two.
The center tube is upright but still too shallow. Regrasp its upper body gently to lift and align it with the neighboring large-hole row.
Lift only a few centimeters to test the center tube regrasp and clear its tip; do not assume retention from the gripper command.
The regrasp did not retain the center tube. Open and approach its body more closely from the front at a lower height, using the wrist view to check engagement.
Narrow the open jaw spacing to clear neighboring caps, level the hand, and lower alongside the central tube body rather than closing above it.
The jaws now surround the center tube's cap region. Close without further downward pressure, then test a short vertical lift for retention.
The cap appears retained on the short lift. Clear the tip and shift slightly right and forward toward the central large opening, keeping the tube upright.
With the cap visibly retained, lower vertically toward the newly centered opening and watch for rim contact before proceeding deeper.
Rim contact persists. Clear it vertically and move the held tube forward to the next large-hole row rather than forcing it down.
Lower the retained third tube vertically at the revised large-slot alignment, stopping short of further pressure if it slips against the rim.
